# `pattern-changed`

Pattern changed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `warn` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `pattern-changed` (both directions), `pattern-changed-in-request`, `pattern-changed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A `pattern` changed. Until regular expressions can be compared, the direction is unknown.

## Why this default

The new pattern may reject old values or produce new ones; it can't be decided from the spec.

## Example

From test case [`pattern-changed`](../../test/cases/pattern-changed/): A pattern changed: the direction cannot be decided.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-           pattern: ^[a-z]+$
+           pattern: ^[a-z0-9]+$
```

Findings:

- `pattern-changed-in-request` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  pattern-changed: warn
```

## How to fix

Check the change by hand.
